title: Passenger comfort and noise impact of UAM (Urban Air Mobility)
summary:
In all sub-studies, artificially made audible, i.e. auralized sounds and sound sequences are presented that can occur in connection with the operation of air cabs. Sub-study 1 focuses on the sounds that can affect passengers in the interior of an air cab cabin. Sub-study 2 deals with the effects that the external noise emitted as a result of over-flights and fly-bys of air cabs can have on local residents.
Age-appropriate normal hearing subjects of male and female gender aged at least 18 years are examined. Before participating in the laboratory study, audiometry will be performed to exclude any test subjects (see exclusion criteria). The test subjects are presented with various auralized sounds via a computer with closed headphones. These are used exclusively in this project, as real-life reference sounds are not yet available.

Sub-study 1, piloting: Two presentations of a total of three sounds from an air taxi cab, each lasting approximately 12 minutes. The sounds presented do not reach a potential-ly harmful continuous sound level. All continuous sound levels are below an LAeqof 75 dB(A). Assessment according to acoustic comfort and speech intelligibility.

Sub-study 1, main test: Two air cab sounds, each about 20 minutes long, were presented twice. The first auralized sound presented twice corresponds to an auralization from the pilot study. This is modified for the second twofold presentation. A maximum level of 75 dB(A) is not exceeded during the sound presentation. Also evaluated accord-ing to acoustic comfort and speech intelligibility.

Sub-study 2: Presentation of six complex scenarios, i.e. the sequence of sounds with a duration of approximately 25 minutes per scenario (= scenario test) and presentation of a maximum of 72 individual sounds with a duration of up to 70 seconds (focused listen-ing test). Evaluation of annoyance and other aspects according to the hypotheses and endpoints (see Outcomes section).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Availability of the signed declaration of consent to data protection, the subject contract, the data protection declaration for the conduct of the study and the subject consent form
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language
- normal hearing for their age
Exclusion criteria:
- Hearing loss in the audiogram: i.e. the hearing thresholds in the better ear are higher than the 10th percentile of the gender- and age-specific hearing thresholds in ISO 7029 (2017)
- Wearing a hearing aid
- Hearing disorders (tinnitus, sudden hearing loss within the last 10 years)
- any medication with an influence on the examination parameters or consumption of stimulants and drugs with an influence on the examination parameters, e.g. drug consumption, increased alcohol consumption and nicotine consumption that does not allow abstinence for at least 10 hours
- persons without legal capacity and persons with limited legal capacity
- do not speak German
- Presence of an acute illness that could impair the attempt and/or lead to infection of other persons
